title: Paid Pomodoro focus timer for students
subtitle: Idea check: a $4.99/month iOS focus timer with nicer design, streaks and study stats.

verdict.summary: The pain is real: students are angry right now at focus apps that added subscriptions, ads and clutter, Forest above all. But the pitch sells features (streaks, stats, design) that Forest, Flora, FocusPomo and FLIP already give away, and a $4.99/month subscription is the exact thing reviewers are rejecting. Pivot the price and the angle: a one-tap, ad-free timer sold once, aimed at people leaving Forest.

opportunities.name: $4.99/mo student focus timer
opportunities.one_liner: Pomodoro timer with nicer design, streaks and study stats, sold as a subscription.
opportunities.why: Pain 6: many different reviewers across six apps, some cancelling or leaving (e5, e12, e18), but every quote comes from one source type (App Store). Willingness to pay 4: people do pay small one-time sums (e13, e19, e20) but push back on subscriptions (e2, e7). Competition gap 3: streaks and stats are already free in strong, well-rated apps (e23, e25, e26, e27). Founder fit 8 and build cost 9: a SwiftUI developer can ship this in weeks for under $500. Reachability 5: App Store search is crowded and student communities could not be verified in this run.

gap.statement: Students who want a simple, good-looking focus timer can't get one that stays out of the way, because the big apps now push subscriptions, ads or clutter on top of the timer.

pains.theme: Subscriptions and paywalls on features people already had
pains.summary: Forest's move to a subscription made paying users feel robbed; other apps paywalled features that used to be free.

pains.theme: Ads in a study app, even after paying
pains.summary: Ads break focus sessions, and some show up after a lifetime purchase.

pains.theme: Bloat: too many taps to start a session
pains.summary: Users want the old one-tap start back and are looking for alternatives.

competitors.positioning: Forest Pro is no longer available to new users.
strengths: Streaks and stats in the free core
weaknesses: Subscription and UI backlash in Sep-Oct 2026 reviews

weaknesses: unknown: review feed empty during this run

weaknesses: unknown: review feed empty during this run

critic.risk: Free incumbents already ship streaks, stats and good design, so the pitch's features are not a reason to pay.
Reviewers in this category reject subscriptions; $4.99/month runs into that.
critic.rebuttal: Only the pivot answers it: sell a one-time unlock, which reviewers say they accept (e2, e13, e19).

critic.risk: App Store discovery is crowded: leaders have 8k to 83k ratings.
Forest could add a classic one-tap mode and win back unhappy users.
Tried and died: no postmortems found. Session reportedly earns about $5k/month (Indie Hackers, page blocked, unverified), so indie timers can work.

win_plan.positioning: A focus timer that starts in one tap. No ads, no subscription.

switching_triggers.move: Be the answer when people ask for a Forest alternative; show one-tap start and pay-once pricing up front.

offers: No ads ever, free tier included
Promise that no feature moves behind a paywall later

build_first.feature: One-tap start and repeat, including from the lock screen

trust: Price shown on the App Store page
stop_doing: Several screens before a session starts

pricing.recommendation: Free, ad-free tier plus a one-time unlock around $4.99 to $9.99
pricing.competitor_range: Free to $19.99 per 3 months; users mention paying $10 lifetime
pricing.rationale: Reviewers pay small one-time sums and reject subscriptions (e2, e13, e19). A monthly price runs into the category's loudest complaint.

validation.experiment: TestFlight beta of a one-tap, ad-free timer, offered to people looking for a Forest alternative.
validation.pass_bar: 100 beta signups and 20 people who say they would pay once
steps: Day 1-3: build one-tap timer with local streaks in SwiftUI
Day 4: TestFlight link and a one-page site
Day 5-7: share it where students ask for Forest alternatives, following each community's rules

kill_criteria: Testers say they would only use it free
